newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico phone regulator warns long-distance firms.
newsitem.headline: Mexico phone regulator warns long-distance firms.

text.p: A Mexican government regulating body said on Monday it could take action if third parties were adversely affected by a current "advertising blitz" by telephone companies competing for the newly opened long-distance market.

"They are within their rights to advertise figures, as long as the data do not affect third parties. (If they do) then the authorities would have to intervene," Pablo Ruiz, spokesman for the Federal Telecommunications Commission (Cofetel), told Reuters.
However, Ruiz did not specify what the sanctions might be.

Competing long-distance companies have released contradictory figures as to the percentage of users they have won over in the central Mexican city of Queretero, where 86,500 voting slips were distributed to telephone customers who were to choose their primary long-distance carrier.
Ruiz said Cofetel would announce the results of those selections on Friday.
Until January 1, Telefonos de Mexico, or Telmex, had enjoyed a monopoly for several decades on long-distance telephone services in Mexico.
